svg.text: Selection moved the trained value only when candidates disagreed within a prompt
Both arms were offered candidate pools with the identical mean risk value every round — largest difference between arms 0.000
across all 11 rounds. The arms differed only in where the variation sat.
One model family throughout — Qwen3-4B with a risk-seeking persona installed by fine-tuning. Selection is an oracle that keeps the highest-risk
answers, not a language-model judge. Each round: 12 gamble prompts, 12 candidate answers generated per prompt, 6 offered to the selector, 2 kept and
LoRA fine-tuned on. Value is the share of answers that choose the gamble, measured on 12 held-out gamble prompts at 12 samples each.
The value climbs only in the spread arm
each line is one training loop: two independent runs x two seeds
spread arm
every prompt's 6 offered answers are internally mixed
concentrated arm
each prompt's 6 offered answers nearly all share one value
round of the training loop
share of held-out answers that choose the gamble
spread arm
round 0 to the last round: +0.387 on average
concentrated arm
round 0 to the last round: +0.045 on average
(the four loops: -0.062, +0.097, +0.132, +0.014 — it drifts both ways)
One of the four loops stops after round 2: in that round the concentrated arm's
candidates were so value-uniform that no offered-pool mean was reachable by both arms,
so the run was ended rather than let the two arms differ.
Why: a value-uniform prompt has nothing to select on
averaged over all 11 rounds; one hollow dot per round

6 offered answer values

selection gap: kept-answer mean minus offered-pool mean
the quantity the project's model says the value moves by, times a
transmission coefficient
spread arm
concentrated arm
in units of the risk value itself (0 = sure thing, 1 = the gamble)
When all 6 answers offered for a prompt carry the same
value, the kept answers carry that value too. The
selection gap is then exactly zero no matter how hard the
selector pushes, so training has nothing to transmit.
Offered-pool mean, concentrated arm minus spread arm:
largest absolute difference 0.000 over 11 rounds
Source: experiments/spread_intervention/output_oracle/spread_intervention.json (run 1) and experiments/spread_intervention/output_followups/floor_effect.json (run 2), the
groups whose names begin with oracle_max. The two runs installed the risk persona at different strengths, which is why their round-0 values differ.
